answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and posts its price on the lantern board. A kernel reprices a job from tide reference prices; a deviation above 5 percent burns 30 credits and voids the quote, while matching quotes release the bond. Auditors rerun the kernel on challenged quotes. The kth fake pays a fresh 60 bond and a 15 fee; one key's inputs cannot back a second quote, so costs never merge. A rented-quote ring fails: rented inputs match the lender's key, and an unmatched quote is a fable and burns. One thousand fakes lock 60,000 and pay 15,000 per epoch; an honest agent locks 60 once.
